_source: Zhao & Caragea, 'EZ-STANCE: A Large Dataset for English Zero-Shot Stance Detection', ACL 2024 (https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.838/). Task sentence verbatim from the abstract / Section 1: 'determine whether the author of a text is in favor, against, or neutral toward a target'. noun_phrase: the stance-labelling instruction given to annotators is verbatim from Appendix C.1 (p. 15708-15709): 'Imagine yourself as the author of the tweet, please annotate the stance that you would take on this given target as “Favor”, “Against”, or “Neutral”.'; C.1 gives no per-label definitions, so the three criteria restate the abstract's task sentence per label. claim: the three label definitions are verbatim from the claim-writing instructions in Appendix C.2 (p. 15709): '1) The author is definitely in favor of the point or message of the claim (favor); 2) The author is definitely against the point or message from the claim (against); 3) Based solely on the information from the tweet, we cannot know whether the author definitely supports or opposes the point or message of the claim (neutral).'
_routing: Each item's target type comes from the release file it was read from (noun_phrase/ vs claim/ directory) and selects the question with the matching key. The state is {"tweet": release `Text`, "target": release `Target 1`}.

noun_phrase.instructions: Zero-shot stance detection: determine whether the author of a text is in favor, against, or neutral toward a target. The state holds a tweet ("tweet") and a noun-phrase target ("target"). Imagine yourself as the author of the tweet, please annotate the stance that you would take on this given target as “Favor”, “Against”, or “Neutral”.

criteria.Favor: The author of the tweet is in favor of the target.
criteria.Against: The author of the tweet is against the target.
criteria.Neutral: The author of the tweet is neutral toward the target.

claim.instructions: Zero-shot stance detection: determine whether the author of a text is in favor, against, or neutral toward a target. The state holds a tweet ("tweet") and a claim target ("target"). Based on the message of the tweet, what is the author's stance toward the point or message of the claim?

criteria.Favor: The author is definitely in favor of the point or message of the claim.
criteria.Against: The author is definitely against the point or message from the claim.
criteria.Neutral: Based solely on the information from the tweet, we cannot know whether the author definitely supports or opposes the point or message of the claim.
